docs.title: formidable
docs.text:
Generate HTML forms from Pydantic models: rendering, parsing, validation, themes and translations, with the model as the single source of truth.

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from werkzeug.wrappers import Response
from formidable.views import Form, trigger


class ContactForm(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(..., title="Your Name")
    age: int = Field(..., title="Age")
    agree: bool = Field(..., title="I agree to terms")
    nickname: str | None = Field(None, title="Nickname (optional)")


class Contact(Form):
    def get_schema(self, request):
        return ContactForm

    @trigger(name="save", title="Save", validate=True)
    def save(self, request, data):
        # `data` is a validated ContactForm instance
        return Response(f"Thanks, {data.name}!")

GET renders the form. POST parses it, validates it and calls the action of the pressed button. If validation fails, the form comes back with the submitted values and an error message at each field.

Which version this describes

This documentation describes the chameleon-rs branch, where all markup lives in Chameleon templates. main does not have these templates, UI schemas or background uploads yet.

docs.title: What's included
docs.text:
• Fields and widgets: every model field becomes a widget, including nested models and repeatable rows.
  • Your own form layout: place each field yourself in a Chameleon template.
  • UI schemas: titles, help texts, units, masks and more, kept apart from the model.
  • Conditional fields: show and hide fields without jQuery.
  • File uploads: with the form, or one by one in the background with FilePond.
  • Themes: Bootstrap 5 and Materialize ship with it.
  • Translations: German error messages included.

CSRF protection is on by default.

docs.title: Conditional fields
docs.text:
Fields can appear depending on other answers, without jQuery or any other dependency:

{
  "attest": {
    "ui:conditions": [
      {"field": "hat_attest", "operator": "equals", "value": "ja"}
    ],
    "ui:condition_logic": "or"
  }
}

The script is only included when a form uses conditions. It clears and disables what is hidden, so browsers don't submit it, and it handles chains of conditions, nested fields and list rows, where a condition looks at its own row first.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text: equals, not_equals, contains, not_contains, starts_with, ends_with, greater_than, less_than, greater_equal, less_equal, empty, not_empty, in, not_in.

docs.title: Requirements still belong in the model
docs.text:
The browser only decides what is visible. A field that is required only under a condition has to be optional in the model, with a validator enforcing the rule:

class Claim(BaseModel):
    hat_attest: t.Literal["ja", "nein"]
    attest_datum: datetime.date | None = None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def attest_needs_a_date(self):
        if self.hat_attest == "ja" and not self.attest_datum:
            raise PydanticCustomError(
                "missing", "Pflichtfeld.", {"field": "attest_datum"})
        return self

See /rueckfrage in ex.py for a real form.

docs.title: Further attributes
docs.text:
These are set through ui:attributes, or directly in your own templates:

Attribute Purpose data-conditions The conditions as ready-made JSON, instead of ui:conditions data-condition-logic or or and data-conditional-options Limits a field's options depending on another answer data-not-required Keeps the field optional when it's shown

docs.title: From JavaScript
docs.text: The script dispatches on change events by itself. After changing values from your own code, call window.FormidableConditions.evaluate().

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
uv sync
uv run pytest
uvx ruff check src/ tests/ ex.py
cd tests/js && npm install && npm test     # the browser scripts

Built on Pydantic v2, chameleon-rs, beartype and werkzeug.

docs.title: This documentation
docs.text:
The pages are in docs/. To preview them:

uvx --from "mkdocs<2" --with mkdocs-material mkdocs serve

A push that changes them publishes the site to GitHub Pages, through the Docs workflow and the gh-pages branch.

docs.title: Bundled FilePond
docs.text: src/formidable/static/filepond/ holds unmodified files from npm, with their versions in VERSIONS. To update them, replace the files and update that list.

docs.title: Fields and widgets
docs.text:
Every field of the model becomes a widget:

Type Widget str Text input int, float, Decimal Number input bool Checkbox date, datetime, time Native date and time inputs SecretStr Password input, never echoed back UploadedFile, FileUpload File input Literal[...], Enum Select list[Literal[...]], list[Enum] Multi-select A nested BaseModel Fieldset list[X] Repeatable rows

X | None makes a field optional. Required fields get the required attribute, labels are linked to their inputs, and defaults and submitted values are filled in.

docs.title: Choosing another widget
docs.text:
You can pick a widget in the model:

bio: str = Field(..., json_schema_extra={"widget": "textarea"})

or, without touching the model, in a UI schema with ui:widget. The names are text, textarea, password, email, radio, select, date, datetime, datetime-local, time, checkbox and file.

docs.title: Nested models and lists
docs.text:
Nesting is encoded in field names as dot paths, such as users.0.name, and folded back into dicts and lists before validation. Indices may have gaps, so deleting a middle row still parses. Pydantic's error locations flatten to the same paths, which puts each error at the right nested input.

List fields get add and remove buttons. A hidden <template> holds a blank row and a small script clones it, with no server round-trip. The script is only included when a form contains a list.

docs.title: Selects and radio groups
docs.text:
Literal[...] and Enum fields render as a <select> with a blank first option, so nothing is preselected by accident. To show them as radio buttons, use ui:widget, or register the widget for the field:

FormRenderer(custom_widgets={"salutation": RadioFieldRenderer})

docs.title: Choices that depend on the request
docs.text:
Build the schema in get_schema(request). It runs for both rendering and validation, so a manipulated POST can't submit an option this request wasn't offered:

def get_schema(self, request):
    flavors = available_flavors(request)   # database, permissions, tenant ...
    return create_model("FlavorForm", __base__=BaseForm,
                        flavor=(t.Literal[flavors], Field(...)))

docs.title: Custom widgets
docs.text:
Register a renderer by type or by dot path:

FormRenderer(
    widgets={TypeHint(str): MyStringRenderer},    # by type
    custom_widgets={"name": MyNameRenderer},      # by dot path
)

A widget receives (name, field_info, field_type, value, errors) and returns markupsafe.Markup. It must render an input under its name, or the field is never submitted. Extending a built-in renderer is the easiest way to get this right, and a new widget can be one line of Python plus a template:

class StarsRenderer(IntFieldRenderer):
    template = "stars.pt"     # found through FormRenderer(templates=[...])

See Changing the markup for how templates are found.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
formidable needs Python 3.12 or newer. It isn't on PyPI, so install it from GitHub:

uv add "formidable @ git+https://github.com/goschtl/formidable@chameleon-rs"

docs.title: A first form
docs.text:
A form is a Pydantic model plus a view. The view is a callable that takes a werkzeug Request and returns a Response, so it fits any WSGI setup. Save this as app.py:

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from werkzeug.serving import run_simple
from werkzeug.wrappers import Request, Response
from formidable.themes import page
from formidable.themes.bootstrap import BOOTSTRAP
from formidable.views import Form, trigger


class ContactForm(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(..., title="Your Name")
    age: int = Field(..., title="Age")


class Contact(Form):
    theme = BOOTSTRAP

    def get_schema(self, request):
        return ContactForm

    def render_response(self, html_form, request):
        return Response(page(html_form, self.get_theme(request), title="Contact"),
                        mimetype="text/html")

    @trigger(name="save", title="Save", validate=True)
    def save(self, request, data):
        return Response(f"Thanks, {data.name}!")


view = Contact()


@Request.application
def app(request):
    return view(request)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_simple("localhost", 8000, app, use_reloader=True)

Run it with uv run python app.py and open http://localhost:8000/. Submit it empty to see the validation errors.

page() wraps the form in a full HTML page with the theme's stylesheets. Without a render_response, the view returns only the <form>, which is what you want when your application has its own page layout.

docs.title: The example application
docs.text:
ex.py in the repository shows nearly everything in this documentation:

git clone -b chameleon-rs https://github.com/goschtl/formidable.git
cd formidable
uv run python ex.py
URL Shows / Nested models, lists and a file upload, in the site-wide theme (Materialize) /material The same form, with the theme set on the view /custom Your own layout in a Chameleon template /rueckfrage A real model with a UI schema and conditions /ui-demo Units, help texts, masks, multiple files /upload-demo Background uploads with FilePond

docs.title: Your own form layout
docs.text: By default the renderer emits the fields one after the other. To arrange them yourself, bind the form and place each piece in a template.

docs.title: In a view
docs.text:
Override get_form and pass the bound form to your template:

from pathlib import Path
from formidable.renderers import render_template

TEMPLATES = Path(__file__).parent / "templates"


class Claim(Form):
    def get_schema(self, request):
        return ClaimForm

    def get_form(self, request, values=None, errors=None):
        return render_template(
            "claim.pt", dirs=(str(TEMPLATES),),
            form=self.bind(request, values, errors))

Validation errors go through get_form as well, so the same template shows them, with no further code.

docs.title: The template
docs.text:
<form tal:attributes="form.attributes">
  ${form.form_errors()}

  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-md-6">${form['name']}</div>
    <div class="col-md-6">${form['email']}</div>
  </div>

  <h2>Address</h2>
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-md-12">${form['address.street']}</div>
    <div class="col-md-4">${form['address.zip']}</div>
    <div class="col-md-8">${form['address.city']}</div>
  </div>

  ${form.buttons()}
</form>
${form.scripts()}

The /custom route in ex.py works like this.

render_template uses formidable's own settings, so novalidate and required render correctly. If you use your own PageTemplateLoader, pass it boolean_attributes=HTML5_BOOLEAN_ATTRIBUTES from chameleon_rs.template.

docs.title: What a bound form offers
docs.text:
form['name'] The whole field: label, input, error, description and help form['address.city'] A field inside a nested model form['users.0.name'] A field inside a list row form['address'] The whole fieldset of a nested model form['name'].title The field's title, honouring ui:title form['name'].name The field's dot path form.attributes The <form> attributes, for tal:attributes form.attrs The same as text, for Jinja2 or f-strings form.form_errors() The block of model-level errors form.error('name') The bare error message of a field form.errors All error messages, by dot path form.buttons() The buttons and the CSRF token form.csrf() Only the CSRF token, if you write your own buttons form.scripts() The scripts and styles the form needs

Looping over form gives the top-level fields in model order:

<div tal:repeat="field form" class="col-md-6">${field}</div>

docs.title: Things to watch out for
docs.text:
Place every field

A field you leave out isn't submitted. If it's required, validation fails, and since the message is rendered with the field, the form comes back with no visible reason. Keep this in mind especially when the model changes.

Keep form.scripts()

List rows, conditions, masks and background uploads all need it.

  • Place a nested field or its fieldset, not both. form['address'] already contains form['address.city'], and the name would be submitted twice.
  • List rows you place yourself are fixed. form['users.0.name'] renders that row, but only form['users'] has the add and remove buttons.
  • Don't name a template variable attrs. Chameleon reserves it.
  • <form ${form.attrs}> doesn't work in Chameleon, because an expression can't stand where an attribute belongs. Use tal:attributes="form.attributes".

docs.title: Other template engines
docs.text:
Fields implement __html__, so Jinja2 doesn't escape them. Jinja2 and plain f-strings can write form.attrs directly into the tag:

f"""<form {form.attrs}>
  {form.form_errors()}
  <div class="left">{form["name"]}</div>
  {form.buttons()}
</form>
{form.scripts()}"""

docs.title: Changing the markup
docs.text:
All markup lives in Chameleon page templates, rendered by chameleon-rs, under src/formidable/templates/formidable/:

<div class="${classes(theme.wrapper)}">
  <label class="${classes(theme.label)}" for="field-${name}">${title}</label>
  <input class="${css}" id="field-${name}" name="${name}" required="${required}"
         step="${step}" type="${input_type}" value="${value}">
  ${render_partial('formidable/error.pt', error=error, theme=theme)}
</div>

To arrange whole fields rather than change their markup, see Your own form layout.

docs.title: Overriding a template
docs.text:
Copy a template and keep its relative path. Your templates beat the theme's, which beat the built-in ones:

FormRenderer(templates=["myapp/templates"])   # myapp/templates/formidable/input.pt
Theme(templates=("mytheme/templates",))       # the same, as part of a theme

docs.title: Writing templates
docs.text:
• Values are HTML-escaped, except for Markup such as rendered fields and partials. Avoid structure: for anything a user can influence.
  • Attributes set to None disappear. required, checked and similar are boolean attributes.
  • classes(...) merges class names and skips empty ones.
  • A template sees the variables its renderer passes, plus theme. A partial only sees what is handed to it.
  • attrs is reserved by Chameleon. The built-in templates use wrapper_attrs and control_attrs for ui:attributes.

docs.title: If your application configures Chameleon
docs.text:
formidable never calls chameleon_rs.configure(), because that setting belongs to your application. If you use it:

  • A formidable/... file in your template_folder overrides the partial of the same name.
  • partial_search="registered" isn't supported, because it hides formidable's own partials.

docs.title: Themes
docs.text:
A Theme bundles what a CSS framework needs: class names for every element, template and widget overrides, and asset URLs. Bootstrap 5 and Materialize ship with formidable.

from formidable import themes
from formidable.themes.bootstrap import BOOTSTRAP
from formidable.themes.material import MATERIAL

themes.use(BOOTSTRAP)                  # the site-wide default, once at startup


class Admin(Form):
    theme = MATERIAL                   # for one view

    def get_theme(self, request):      # or per request, for multi-tenant sites
        ...

page(html_form, theme, title=...) wraps a form in a full HTML page with the theme's stylesheets and scripts. Without a theme, the output is clean HTML with stable classes that you can style yourself.

docs.title: Writing a theme
docs.text: src/formidable/themes/bootstrap.py is a complete example and only about 30 lines. Set class names on a Theme, and add templates where class names aren't enough.

docs.title: Translations
docs.text:
Pydantic identifies errors by stable type strings. A catalog maps them to message templates, with {placeholders} filled from the error context. A German catalog ships as formidable.i18n.GERMAN, and unknown types fall back to Pydantic's English.

from formidable import i18n

i18n.use({**i18n.GERMAN, "nickname_required": "..."})   # site-wide


class Kontakt(Form):
    error_messages = {...}                  # for one view

    def get_messages(self, request):        # or per request, by Accept-Language
        ...

Your own PydanticCustomError types translate the same way.

The labels of the upload widget are separate: pass i18n.UPLOAD_GERMAN as upload_options, see File uploads.

docs.title: UI schemas
docs.text:
A ui_schema.json adds presentation to a model without touching it. It maps dot paths to ui:* entries, with items standing in for list rows:

{
  "kosten": {"ui:unit": "EUR", "ui:help": "Bitte Belege beifügen."},
  "users.items.street": {"ui:title": "Straße"}
}

from formidable.ui import load_ui, parse_ui

FormRenderer(ui=load_ui("ui_schema.json"))
FormRenderer(ui=parse_ui({"kosten": {"ui:unit": "EUR"}}))   # or from a dict

A UI schema decides how a field looks, never whether its value is valid. That stays with the model. Unknown keys are ignored.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Key Purpose ui:title Replaces the field's title ui:description Replaces the field's description ui:placeholder The input's placeholder ui:widget Another widget ui:options Choices with labels, as a list of {"value": ..., "label": ...} ui:help A help text below the field, escaped ui:unit A unit next to the input ui:mask Formats input while typing, see below ui:multiple Lets a file input take several files ui:accept Filters the file dialog, as a list of mime types ui:attributes Any further attributes, see below ui:conditions Shows and hides the field ui:condition_logic or (the default) or and

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
ui:attributes go on the input, select or textarea, and on the fieldset of nested models and lists. An attribute replaces a value the template already sets, so class replaces the theme's classes.

data-conditions, data-condition-logic, data-conditional-options and data-not-required go on the element around the field, where the conditions script reads them.

docs.title: Masks
docs.text:
{"nummer": {"ui:widget": "text",
            "ui:mask": {"mask": "99-9999", "mask_placeholder": "#"}}}

9 stands for a digit, a for a letter and * for either; anything else is inserted as it is. The mask also becomes the placeholder, here ##-####.

A mask needs a ui:widget

Without a ui:widget, the mask is ignored, as it is in deform.

A mask only helps while typing, so validate the value in the model as well. An incomplete value stays in the field and the model rejects it on submit.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: ui:multiple needs a list in the model, and ui:accept is only a filter that users can bypass, so check content types on the server if they matter. See File uploads.

docs.title: File uploads
docs.text:
There are two ways to handle files. The model decides which one a field uses.

With the form In the background Model field UploadedFile, FileUpload str, list[str] Needs Nothing An upload URL in your application After a validation error Choose the files again Files stay Progress, drag and drop No Yes Requires JavaScript No Yes

docs.title: With the form
docs.text:
formidable.fields has two types:

  • UploadedFile is werkzeug's FileStorage, with .stream, .filename, .content_type and .save(path). Large uploads are spooled to disk, so prefer it for anything sizeable.
  • FileUpload is the content read into bytes, for small files.
class Claim(BaseModel):
    belege: list[UploadedFile] = Field(default_factory=list, title="Belege")

With {"ui:widget": "file", "ui:multiple": true} in the UI schema, users can choose several files. The form gets enctype="multipart/form-data" automatically, and an empty file input counts as not submitted.

Browsers can't fill in file inputs, so if another field fails validation, users are told to choose their files again. Set max_content_length on your request class to limit the total size.

docs.title: In the background
docs.text:
With an upload URL, a file field holding references uploads each file as soon as it's chosen, through the bundled FilePond. The form then submits only the ids, and the files come back after a validation error.

class Claim(BaseModel):
    belege: list[str] = Field(..., title="Belege")


FormRenderer(
    ui=parse_ui({"belege": {"ui:widget": "file", "ui:multiple": True,
                            "ui:accept": ["application/pdf", "image/png"]}}),
    upload_url="/upload",
    upload_options=i18n.UPLOAD_GERMAN,   # German labels, or any FilePond option
)

A reference field needs an upload URL

Without upload_url, a list[str] file field renders a plain file input, and fails validation on submit.

docs.title: The upload URL
docs.text:
Storing files is up to your application. The URL has to handle:

Request Purpose Response POST Store the file, sent as a multipart part named like the field The id, as plain text DELETE Remove a file; the id is the request body Empty GET ?id= Give a file back The file, with its name in Content-Disposition

The CSRF token arrives in an X-CSRF-Token header. Uploads in ex.py is a small example, which you can try at /upload-demo. It keeps its list of files in memory, so don't use it as it is.

docs.title: What your endpoint must do
docs.text:
Ids are user input

Generate ids on the server, and check on submit that they belong to the user. Otherwise anyone can post someone else's id and claim that file.

  • Check size and type on the server. The browser checks are a convenience and can be bypassed.
  • Remove abandoned files. Forms that are never submitted leave their uploads behind, as does a file in a field that gets hidden again.

docs.title: Limits in the browser
docs.text:
ui:accept limits the type and data-max-file-size in ui:attributes the size:

{"attest": {"ui:widget": "file",
            "ui:accept": ["application/pdf"],
            "ui:attributes": {"data-max-file-size": "2MB"}}}

Use mime types in ui:accept, not file extensions.

docs.title: Page size
docs.text: FilePond is part of the form rather than a separate file, which adds about 140 KB to each page that uses it. No third-party server is involved.

docs.title: Validation and errors
docs.text:
Pydantic is the only validator. Forms render with novalidate, so the browser never blocks a submit; FormRenderer(novalidate=False) turns browser validation back on.

Before validation, HTML form quirks are normalized:

  • Unchecked checkboxes become False.
  • Empty submissions are dropped. Optional fields fall back to their defaults, and required ones fail as missing rather than as an unparsable empty string.

docs.title: Where errors appear
docs.text:
Errors are routed by dot path to the exact widget, as a message plus an invalid class on the input. Errors from a model-level validator appear at the top of the form, unless they name a field:

@model_validator(mode="after")
def nickname_required_when_agreeing(self):
    if self.agree and not self.nickname:
        raise PydanticCustomError(
            "nickname_required",
            "When agreeing to the terms, a nickname is required.",
            {"field": "nickname"})   # appears at the nickname widget
    return self

Several errors at once work too. Raise them with ValidationError.from_exception_data, each with its own field. See ex_forms/LD_000_0V1100/model.py in the repository.

Regular expressions with lookaround need Python's engine:

model_config = ConfigDict(regex_engine="python-re")

docs.title: Views and buttons
docs.text: A view subclasses formidable.views.Form. GET renders the form and POST handles a submit.

docs.title: Buttons
docs.text:
Buttons are methods, marked with @trigger:

@trigger(name="save", title="Save", validate=True, order=0)
def save(self, request, data): ...

@trigger(name="draft", title="Save draft", order=1)
def draft(self, request, data): ...

With validate=True, the action receives the validated model instance, and validation errors re-render the form automatically. Without it, the action gets the raw, normalized data, which suits buttons that work on incomplete input.

A button value can carry an argument: value="remove:3" calls action(request, data, "3").

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
Override these methods to change how a view behaves:

Hook Purpose get_schema(request) The model get_renderer(request) Widgets, theme, UI schema, upload URL, novalidate get_theme(request) Theme selection; falls back to themes.use() get_messages(request) Error messages; falls back to i18n.use() get_form(request, values, errors) The assembled form; override for your own layout bind(request, values, errors) A bound form, for your own layout render_response(html_form, request) The page around the form get_csrf_token(request) Where the CSRF token comes from

docs.title: The renderer
docs.text:
get_renderer returns a FormRenderer, which takes:

Argument Purpose theme The theme; defaults to the site-wide one ui A UI schema widgets Widgets by type custom_widgets Widgets by dot path templates Folders with template overrides novalidate True by default; False turns browser validation back on upload_url Where background uploads go upload_options Further FilePond options

docs.title: CSRF protection
docs.text:
CSRF protection is on by default and uses the double-submit cookie pattern. A hidden __csrf__ field must match the formidable-csrf cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax), and a mismatch gets a 403. It needs no session storage.

Set csrf = False on a view if your framework already protects it. A hand-written form gets the token from form.buttons().
